name: Atlanta
lede: From the friendliest par-3 course in the region to a championship-caliber test near downtown — Atlanta's four published courses cover every level. We're publishing the metro's best first.
introParagraphs: Atlanta disc golf spans the whole spectrum. Oregon Park in Marietta is the region's favorite beginner course — 18 gentle par 3s where a huge slice of Atlanta's players took their first putts. Little Mulberry in Dacula is the wooded technical step up, and East Roswell's tight fairways and hills teach accuracy the hard way.
Perkerson Park near downtown is the championship test — a John Ritger design that the locals call the most challenging of the city's top tracks. All four of our published Atlanta courses are free.
New here? Oregon Park to learn, then Little Mulberry, then Perkerson when you're ready.

faqs.question: How many disc golf courses are in the Atlanta metro?
faqs.answer: Around 55 courses across the metro. We're publishing the best first — 4 are live today, with more added every week.

faqs.question: What's the best disc golf course in Atlanta?
faqs.answer: Little Mulberry in Dacula is the highest-rated published course, but Perkerson Park near downtown is the one serious players measure themselves against.

faqs.question: Are Atlanta's disc golf courses free?
faqs.answer: Yes — all four of our published courses (Oregon Park, Little Mulberry, East Roswell, Perkerson) are free to play.

faqs.question: What's the best beginner course in Atlanta?
faqs.answer: Oregon Park in Marietta — the friendliest par-3 course in the region and where most local players started.
